about: Assembly steps for the 3D viewer, following docs/3d/assembly.md. Each step adds parts (ids from the model) that slide in from `from` (mm, CAD frame: +x robot's front, +y robot's left, +z up). Parts added earlier stay in place.

steps.title: Start with the head shell
steps.text: Take the printed Head. The OLED pocket faces the front.

steps.title: Seat the OLED
steps.text: Peel the protective sticker and plug the OLED cable in first: once the display is in its pocket, the connector is hard to reach. Then seat the OLED in the front pocket.

steps.title: Seat the head servo
steps.text: Take one of the five servos, no horn yet. Seat it in its pocket. Route the OLED cable out one side of the head and the servo lead out the other, and clip both into the clips on the back.

steps.title: Close the head with the hat
steps.text: Place Hat on top of Head and fasten with two M2×8 screws. Do not overtighten.

sections.title: Neck: center a servo and attach Neck

steps.title: Center the neck servo
steps.text: Take the next servo, no horn. Plug it into the board and use Assembly support → Move all to 90° so the shaft is at its center.

steps.title: Press Neck onto the shaft
steps.text: Press Neck onto the servo shaft, perpendicular to the servo body, with the bulge in the middle of Neck toward the back of the servo (the cable end). Fasten with the screw that came with the servo.

steps.title: Drop in the nut
steps.text: Put an M2 nut in the hex pocket with the larger hole, on the robot's right. Leave the other pocket empty. Unplug the servo.

steps.title: Fit Neck onto the head servo
steps.text: Center the head servo. Fit Neck onto the head servo shaft (Neck has a pocket for it), then slide it on until the nut side sits flush with Head. At 90°, Neck must be perpendicular to Head.

steps.title: Fasten both sides
steps.text: Robot's right: M2×8 into the captured nut. Robot's left: the screw that came with the servo. Unplug the head servo.

steps.title: Take the chest
steps.text: The cable tunnels are at the front of Chest.

steps.title: Seat the robot's left servo
steps.text: Seat a servo in the left side pocket, no horn. Route the lead through the vertical tunnel at the front so it exits at the bottom. Fasten with two M2×16 screws.

steps.title: Seat the robot's right servo
steps.text: Same on the right side: lead through the front tunnel, two M2×16 screws.

sections.title: Mount the head assembly on Chest

steps.title: Route the neck servo lead
steps.text: Before seating it, route the neck servo's lead through the central tunnel in Chest and out the bottom.

steps.title: Seat the neck servo in the center pocket
steps.text: Keep the front of Head and Neck on the front of Chest (the side with the tunnels). Fasten with M2×8 screws: two if they fit, otherwise one at the back.

steps.title: Center the last servo
steps.text: Take the last servo and center it at 90°.

steps.title: Press BellyJoint onto the shaft
steps.text: No horn. Seat the hexagonal BellyJoint so one flat edge is parallel to the short side of the servo body. Fasten with the servo screw, then unplug the servo.

sections.title: Route chest cables through Belly and join

steps.title: Thread the three leads
steps.text: Pass the three leads from the bottom of Chest (left hand, neck, right hand) into Belly through the large upper opening and out through the lower side opening. Keep their left-to-right order.

steps.title: Fasten Belly to Chest
steps.text: Rounded side of Belly to the back, matching the profile of Chest. Four M2×8 screws.

steps.title: Chair
steps.text: Take Chair.

steps.title: Seat the body servo
steps.text: Seat the servo with BellyJoint in the pocket at the bottom of Chair. Route its lead out under Chair and forward through the center channel.

steps.title: Slide the seats on, not all the way
steps.text: Slide SeatLeft and SeatRight onto the dovetails from the sides. Leave a gap so BellyJoint stays clear.

steps.title: Lower the body onto BellyJoint
steps.text: Lower Belly (with everything above it) onto BellyJoint: its base has a matching hex pocket. Then push the seats together to lock it. Do not pinch the cables. Optionally fasten the seats with two M2×16 screws.

steps.title: Desk
steps.text: Take Desk.

steps.title: Nest DeskTop in DeskPad
steps.text: Seat DeskTop into DeskPad.

steps.title: Fasten the stack to Desk
steps.text: Rounded cutout toward the robot. Four M2×16 screws through the corner holes.

steps.title: Fasten AiEmblem to the front
steps.text: Two short M2×4 screws.

steps.title: Seat the main control board
steps.text: Seat the board in the desk cavity. Leave servos and OLED unplugged for now. Connect the speaker and tuck it inside the desk.

steps.title: Seat the ESP32-C3-Zero from above
steps.text: Pins through the desk-top cut into the board headers; orient by the USB marking. It sits flush. Optional: power on the board USB-C and check that the setup access point starts, then power down.

steps.title: LampButton under LampBase
steps.text: Place LampButton under LampBase so it can press the ESP32 reset button.

steps.title: Fasten LampBase
steps.text: Opening over the ESP32 status LED. Two M2×8 screws; this also holds the ESP32.

steps.title: Laptop
steps.text: Slide LaptopScreen into the pocket under LaptopCase. Place the laptop on the desk and fasten with one M2×8 from under the desk.

steps.title: Mug
steps.text: Seat Coffee in Mug, place the mug on its spot, one M2×8 from under the desk.

steps.title: Bell
steps.text: Drive an M2×16 fully into Bell first, then drive it down into the desk and secure it with a nut underneath.

steps.title: Plug in by channel
steps.text: Tip the desk onto its front wall. Channel 0 head pitch, 1 neck yaw, 2 left hand, 3 right hand, 4 body. Plug the OLED in too, then power up for a servos + OLED smoke test.

sections.title: Fasten Chair to Desk, close the underside

steps.title: Join Chair and Desk
steps.text: Slide the desk up to the chair until the holes line up. Six M2×8 screws, three per side. Keep cables out of the screw paths.

steps.title: BottomCover
steps.text: Turn the robot over without loading the arms or props. Keep cables inside the perimeter. Fasten BottomCover with six M2×8 pan-head screws (heads ≤ 4.0 × 2.0 mm): four into the desk, two into the chair.

steps.title: Left elbow
steps.text: Fasten ForearmLeft to an UpperArm with one M2×8 screw.

steps.title: Right elbow
steps.text: Fasten ForearmRight to the other UpperArm with one M2×8 screw.

steps.title: Mount the arms on the chest servos
steps.text: Center the hand servos. Press each arm onto its shaft (the upper arms have pockets for them), hand at shoulder height and forearm pointing toward the desk. Fasten with the servo screws.

steps.title: Cap on diffuser, into LampBase
steps.text: No screws. Put LampCap on LampDiffuser and push the stack into LampBase.

steps.title: Built
steps.text: Power on, join the TinyEngineer-XXXX access point, open http://192.168.4.1/config and walk through the whole setup wizard: servo calibration, OLED, LED, speaker, Wi-Fi.
